claim.summary: Over any field, let literal CNF violation products F_i and all Boolean B_j=x_j^2-x_j have Hilbert-like certificate C(x,Y,Z), size S depth d. Put P=product_i(1-F_i), P_i=product_(k!=i)(1-F_k), and literal-telescoping T_i(x,B)=F_i^2-F_i. Then Q=C(x,(-P_i T_i(x,Z))_i,(P Z_j)_j) satisfies Q(x,B)=P, is Hilbert-like and has size O(S+s^3), depth<=d+10, s=m+n+literal length+1, counting gates and wires with unbounded fan-in. Conversely sum_i(product_(k<i)(1-F_k))Y_i+Q gives a certificate with fixed clause coefficients, size O(S+s^3), depth<=max(d,6)+2. Repeated, tautological and empty clauses allowed; polynomial Hilbert-likeness suffices.
claim.assessment: Working explicit formal transformation, medium reviewed. Extends the earlier selector identity by retaining and constructing Boolean corrections from the supplied certificate. Does not supply a certificate from nothing, preserve exact Frege simulation image or give a PC degree bound.

claim.summary: For every identity P=sum_j b_j(x)(x_j^2-x_j) over any field, b_j(a)=(2a_j-1)partial_j P(a) at every Boolean a. All Boolean-point coefficient values are syzygy invariant. For a literal CNF satisfaction product P, r_j=(2x_j-1)partial_jP jointly represent these values with size O(s^3), depth<=8 via the literal product rule. These representatives need not be formal correction coefficients; duplicated inconsistent units give P=B^2, b=B, all traces zero but P formally nonzero.

claim.summary: For any literal CNF satisfaction product H(x_1,...,x_r), append contradictory units on fresh z. Its satisfaction product P=-(z^2-z)H has explicit small constant-depth Boolean certificate Q=-H Z_z. Ordered monic division by B_1,...,B_r,B_z, passing each remainder onward, has final coefficient -ML(H). Thus universal efficient canonical-coefficient extraction even from supplied small certificates would efficiently multilinearize arbitrary CNF satisfaction products.
claim.assessment: Working explicit all-parameter projection, checked by same medium reviewer. A conditional complexity implication, not an unconditional hardness result. A difficult canonical coefficient does not imply certificate hardness, since these padded CNFs have explicit cheap certificates.

claim.summary: For any unsatisfiable binary CNF with no empty clause and q a power of two, clause coefficients A_i=f_i^(q-1) product_(j<i)(1-f_j^q) give sum A_i f_i=1-P^q, P=product(1-f_i) nonzero formally. The residual has every Hasse derivative of order less than q zero at all Boolean points. These are constant-depth arithmetic candidates of size polynomial in q and CNF length, but not IPS certificates.
claim.assessment: Symbolic telescoping/Frobenius control of fixed-order jet shortcuts. Does not obstruct tests whose order exceeds the candidate degree or supply Boolean correction coefficients.

claim.summary: Over any field, for a polynomial-ring retraction rho with rho(F0)=1, every Hilbert-like certificate sum c_i F_i=1 has a Koszul-syzygy-equivalent representative with rho(C')=Y0: c'_i=c_i-rho(c_i)F0 for i>0 and c'_0=c0+sum_(i>0)rho(c_i)F_i. For a coordinate restriction, a size-S depth-d circuit and shared generator size G/depth Delta yield size O((q+1)S+G+q+1), depth at most max(d,Delta)+4 and coefficient degree at most L+g. Applied to Boolean matrix rank with B=0, the entire restricted certificate is one placeholder, including all Boolean coefficients.
claim.assessment: Elementary explicit normalization, valid for polynomial Hilbert-likeness without syntactic linearity. The degree/circuit bounds concern coordinate restrictions; a general retraction has only the algebraic assertion. This defeats the specified universal zero-factor coefficient extraction, not all certificate-size methods or general IPS.
